_comment: Non-secret defaults for local development. In Azure Container Apps every value below is
supplied as an environment variable or an ACA secret (Key Vault reference), so this file
should NOT carry a broker credential or a connection string.
Names match the migration plan's configuration contract (section 2.3).
_layout: Settings tree, resolved relative to AppContext.BaseDirectory (the build/publish output),
NOT the process working directory. Deploy-WwQueueProcessor.ps1 BAKES this tree into the
container image (no volume mount, no startup fetch - a scale-to-zero worker would pay that
Settings/triggers/<triggerId>.bite   Queue-trigger definition(s). Stage exactly one, or
stage several and set QUEUE:TRIGGERID - the loader
refuses to guess which queue this app serves.
Settings/sources/<sourceId>.bite     Every source the trigger references - both
scanning for a *.bite whose ID attribute matches, so
an operator-named Studio file also works.
Settings/ itself is still searched for sources AFTER Settings/sources/, for compatibility
with the earlier flat layout and the engine's Settings/ElasticsearchLoggingSource.bite.
Committed sample (copied to bin/ on build, deliberately NOT published into the image - see
_comment_empty_values: An empty string below means UNSET, not 'use empty'. Program.cs reads these with
ReadString/IsNullOrWhiteSpace, so a placeholder can never beat the code default.
QUEUE:TRIGGERFILTER) take their defaults from QueueProcessorOptions and are overridden
per-deployment with the QUEUE__* environment variables.

_TENANTID: Set by Deploy-WwQueueProcessor.ps1 -TenantId (defaulted from `az account show`).
Leave UNSET only for a system-assigned managed identity, where the tenant is implied.
A user-assigned MI, the local az CLI credential, or a client secret all REQUIRE it -
without it the credential chain fails with 'Invalid tenant id provided', which reads
like a missing app role rather than missing config. The worker warns at startup.

_comment_concurrency: MAXCONCURRENCY 1 is the measured on-prem behaviour: dispatch is serial per channel, so one
replica runs one workflow at a time. Keep the trigger's Prefetch equal to it - a higher
prefetch only parks messages in this replica where other replicas cannot take them, which
starves scale-out and widens the redelivery window on drain. Scale OUT (maxReplicas =
trigger Concurrency, minReplicas = 0), do not scale UP in-replica.
